thread:
rachel: deploy-bot flagged a canary regression after we promoted v4.0.0 to router-service. p95 jumped and error-rate spiked. deploy-bot suggests autorevert to v3.9.4. change window ends 23:45 UTC. requesting manual hold + decision.
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary router-service p95=980ms (baseline 300ms), errors 0.7% -> 3.4%. autorevert candidate: v3.9.4. evidence: https://telemetry.redwood/canary/4078
tom: quick check — are any Dedicated lanes pinned to v4.0.0? don't want to auto-revert something customers expect.
rachel: one EU dedicated customer was migrated yesterday but they are pinned to v3.9.x for now. hosted only on canary slice. product-ops prepping blurb.
dave: infra shows increased KV eviction on router-eu-03 and higher disk iops. no OOMs. looks like cache churn from the new batching heuristic in v4.0.0.
mira: that matches a spike in background compaction logs. could be compaction vs kvcache interplay.
oncall-ops: change window 22:30-00:30 UTC. canary slice is 12%. deploy-bot threshold hit — we can let autorevert run, but manual hold recommended while product and CSMs get briefed.
rachel: suppressing autorevert for 7m to validate: `deployctl suppress-autorevert --service router-service --for 7m`
dave: good. can someone run a targeted smoke and kvcache metrics?
mira: running smoke: `curl -sS https://router.int/canary/health | jq .p95,.error_rate` -> p95 990ms, errors 3.1%. kvcache hit-rate down 18% vs baseline.
tom: OK looks like regression tied to cache warming. if we rollback we'll lose traces but reduce customer impact. product-ops: ready with blurb?
csm-ops: drafting: "We detected a short-lived performance regression during a canary deploy and rolled back the release. No customer data affected; we'll provide an engineering update once available." sending to CSMs now.
legal: cc. file an incident ticket if rollback executed. include timeline and customer blurb.
rachel: requesting manual approve to rollback. assigning @dave to run revert and @mira to validate. rollback command below.
dave: executing in 1m. pausing autoscale for canary pool: `infractl autoscale set router-canary --min 0 --max 0`
dave: running: ```release rollback --service router-service --to v3.9.4 --strategy rolling --slice 12 --reason "canary p95 regression"```
deploy-bot: ACTION: rollback initiated by dave. progress: 10% -> 45% -> 85% -> 100%.
mira: after 60% rolled back p95 dropped to 360ms, errors 0.9%. kvcache hit-rate climbing.
csm-ops: customer blurb sent to CSMs.
legal: incident ticket created: INC-2026-4078. no SLA breach expected, will update if anything changes.
dave: re-enabling autoscale: `infractl autoscale set router-canary --min 1 --max 6`
mira: running post-rollback validation: smoke checks green, one long-tail trace captured for RCA. saving traces.
rachel: release notes snippet: "Canary regression detected; automated system recommended rollback; manual authorization executed. Rolled back to v3.9.4; monitoring ongoing." will publish when ops confirms.
oncall-ops: monitoring for 1h with tightened p95 alert for canary. temporary alert rule created.
mira: assigning RCA to mira+dave. we'll look at kvcache heuristics, compaction interplay, and kernel selector pathing. ETA preliminary findings 6 hours.
rachel: thanks all. rollback executed, customers notified, ops monitoring. closing thread after 1h stable. :white_check_mark:
